report.summary: Chunk 6 defines dataclasses GateResult, PatchArtifact, AttemptResult, and a partial Attempt dataclass. Claims about containment, diff encoding, and ledger trimming are partially checkable.
risks: GateResult.containment | medium | Field containment is typed as ContainmentAttestation but default is None; code elsewhere may assume it's non-None. | Add a check that all gate results from the runner have containment set.

PatchArtifact.diff | low | The docstring warns that decode round-trip can corrupt non-UTF-8 diffs; this property uses 'replace' which may mask errors. | Verify that callers never use .diff for persistence.
AttemptResult.state | medium | Field state is a string with no documented enum; consumers may rely on specific values not defined here. | Define allowed state constants or document expected values.
todos: Add a sentinel or default for GateResult.containment to avoid None ambiguity.
Consider making AttemptResult.state an Enum or Literal type.
Verify that GATE_OUTPUT_TAIL_CHARS is defined in the module.

claims.text: A gate verdict with its raw output kept, not summarised.
claims.why: The class stores output, returncode, duration, etc., and provides a summary() method that trims output, but the raw output is kept in the 'output' field.

claims.text: EFFECTIVE containment, not the request -- see :class:`daedalus.spine.containment.ContainmentAttestation`. A verdict on candidate code is only worth as much as the boundary it ran behind, so the boundary that ACTUALLY held travels with the verdict into the ledger. ``None`` only for a gate result some other code path constructed.
claims.why: The comment references ContainmentAttestation from another module; its semantics cannot be verified from this chunk.

claims.text: The trimmed view written to the ledger (see GATE_OUTPUT_TAIL_CHARS).
claims.why: GATE_OUTPUT_TAIL_CHARS is not defined in this chunk; its existence and value are unknown.

claims.text: A candidate change as inert data. Nothing here applies itself.
claims.why: The class only holds data fields and provides properties; it has no method to apply the patch.

claims.text: ``diff_bytes`` is authoritative and ``diff_sha256`` is taken over it; a human promoting the patch should write those bytes, not the decoded ``diff``, because a decode round-trip can corrupt a diff containing bytes that are not valid UTF-8.
claims.why: The class stores diff_bytes and diff_sha256; the diff property decodes with 'replace', which can change bytes, confirming the warning.

claims.text: Convenience view for humans and logs; not the digested form.
claims.why: The property decodes to string and is not used for persistence; the docstring accurately describes it.

claims.text: The complete, exception-free outcome of one attempt.
claims.why: The class contains fields for state, timestamps, artifact, gates, errors; it represents the outcome of an attempt without exceptions being raised.

observations.what: GateResult.containment has type ContainmentAttestation but defaults to None; the comment says None only for other code paths, but no validation ensures it's set.
PatchArtifact.diff property uses 'replace' error handling, which may silently corrupt non-UTF-8 data; the docstring warns but does not prevent misuse.
AttemptResult.state is a plain string with no documented set of values; callers may rely on specific strings not defined here.
GateResult.summary uses GATE_OUTPUT_TAIL_CHARS which is not defined in this chunk; may cause NameError at runtime.
